items.title: Multi-page browse: follow pagination / 'next' / 'load more' to gather N results across pages
items.why: anvil browse/scrape reads ONE page only (grep pagination|load more|next page = 0 in agent.ts + anvil.ts). A 'find the 5 cheapest flights' / 'newest 20 listings' errand only ever sees page-one results — the exact multi-page loop the competitor (Instinct) sells. A texting user asking for 'the 10 cheapest' silently gets whatever fit on one screen.
items.how: Add a bounded page-follow to the browse/find path: after reading a page, detect a next/pagination control (rel=next, a 'Next'/'More'/numbered pager, or an anchor whose text matches /next|more|older/), click it, accumulate results, cap at ~3-5 pages + a hard time budget. Reuse src/anvil.ts click+read. New tool arg or a 'depth'/'pages' hint. Offline unit test with a mock 2-page site + a LIVE e2e against a real paginated listing (e.g. HN news?p=2). Report items-gathered > page-one count.

items.title: Full-page screenshot (not just the viewport fold)
items.why: anvil.ts:463 captures the VIEWPORT only — 'screenshot the whole page' / 'screenshot this article' gives just the top fold, surprising a user who expected the full page.
items.how: Add a fullPage option to the screenshot capture in src/anvil.ts (CDP captureBeyondViewport / Page.captureScreenshot with fromSurface+full metrics, or puppeteer fullPage:true). Route 'whole/full/entire page' phrasing to it in the agent's screenshot dispatch; keep viewport as the default (smaller, faster). Live e2e: assert full-page bytes are materially larger than viewport for a long page.

items.title: Surface stoppedEarly on the non-/run chain paths (digest members, index.ts:174/211/970)
items.why: The interactive /run path (handler.ts:1737) flags a partial chain, but the digest-member + other index.ts call sites take bare .final and DROP stoppedEarly — a chain that failed a step mid-way is presented to the user as if it completed, in a daily briefing. Silent-wrong = trust erosion.
items.how: Thread stoppedEarly/step-counts through the digest-member runChain (index.ts:174) + the other .final call sites (211, 970) and have the digest/caller append a short '(partial — N of M steps)' note, mirroring handler.ts:1737. Offline unit test: a 2-step chain whose 2nd step returns degraded shows the partial note.

items.title: Infinite-scroll capture: scroll a feed to load more items before reading
items.why: Feeds/listings that load on scroll (not pagination) yield only the initial ~10 items to a single read — a 'what's new on <scrolling feed>' errand under-reports.
items.how: Add a bounded scroll-to-load to the browse path in src/anvil.ts: repeat scrollBy(0, viewport) + wait-for-network-idle up to K times or until item count stops growing, then read. Cap iterations + time. Live e2e against a real infinite-scroll page; assert post-scroll item count > initial.

items.title: Structured extraction across paginated/scrolled results (rows, not a text wall)
items.why: scrape_pages + scroll_feed now GATHER multiple pages, but return raw concatenated text — for "the 5 cheapest" / "20 newest listings" the model must re-parse a big blob, which is lossy + token-heavy. Extracting structured rows (title/price/url) across the gathered pages is the actual competitor-grade listing errand.
items.how: Add a paged/scrolled variant to the extract path (or a fields option on scrape_pages/scroll_feed) that runs the existing per-item extraction over each gathered page and returns a deduped JSON array capped at the requested N. Reuse extract.ts + the multi-page gatherers. Offline unit test with a mock 2-page listing; live e2e asserting N rows across pages.

items.title: Full-page PDF: "save the whole article/thread as a PDF" captures everything, not one print-page
items.why: pdf() renders via anvil /v1/pdf; like screenshot before the fullPage fix, a long thread/article likely gets clipped to default print pagination. A user saving a long page expects the whole thing. Mirror the screenshot-fullpage win.
items.how: Check anvil /v1/pdf options (printBackground, preferCSSPageSize, scale, full-content). Thread a fullPage/complete flag through relay pdf(url,full) + the pdf tool dispatch when the user says whole/entire/full. Live e2e: full PDF byte size materially larger for a long page.

items.title: extract_list should also gather from an infinite-scroll feed (not just pagination)
items.why: extract_list gathers via scrapePaged (pagination links) only. A scroll-loaded feed (no next link) would still extract just the first screen of rows. Pairing it with scrapeScroll closes the gap for feeds like listings/job boards that lazy-load.
items.how: Add a source hint (or auto-detect: if scrapePaged returns pages=1, try scrapeScroll) to extract_list so it can gather from a scrolling feed before the row extraction. Reuse scrapeScroll. Live e2e on a real infinite-scroll listing.

items.title: extract_list can hand back a CSV/spreadsheet file (like compare does)
items.why: compare already offers "as a CSV" -> a spreadsheet file. extract_list returns a JSON array of rows the user often wants to KEEP (20 listings, prices). A CSV export is the natural save for a list, and the rows are already structured.
items.how: When the user says csv/spreadsheet/export, serialize the extract_list rows to CSV (reuse the compare CSV path / a shared rows-to-csv helper) and attach as a doc. Header = fields; one row per item. Unit test the CSV shape; live e2e optional.

items.title: Click-driven "Load more" BUTTON support in the multi-page browse path
items.why: scrapePaged follows <a href> pagers and scrapeScroll handles scroll, but a <button>Load more</button>/<button>Show more</button> that fetches + appends items (very common on listings/job boards/product grids) is neither — the browse tools still get only the first batch.
items.how: In scrapeScroll (or a variant), after each scroll also try clicking a visible button/anchor whose text matches load more|show more|see more (reuse the wants regex, in-page click via evaluate), wait for content to grow, repeat under the same cap+budget. Live e2e on a real load-more listing; assert item count grows past the first batch.

items.title: extract_list dedup should consider all fields, not just the first
items.why: extractListResult dedups by the first field's value only, so two distinct items that share a title (different price/date) collapse to one — a real listing (two tickets same event, different price) loses rows.
items.how: Dedup by a composite key of ALL requested field values (JSON.stringify the normalized row) instead of just field[0]. Keep the all-null skip. Update the dedup unit test.

history.note: Fixed the non-/run chain paths presenting a stopped-early chain as if it completed. digest-runner now takes a STRUCTURED runChain result: a member chain that stopped early (failed/degraded step or unmet if-gate) is shown as "(partial — N of M steps) ..." AND counted as failed (so an all-partial digest hits the honest all-failed notice, not a silent half-answer). index.ts: digest dep (174) returns the structured result; trigger-to-action (211) + "Run again" (970) return null on stoppedEarly (like a degraded run) instead of attaching a partial. The /run path + scheduler already surfaced it. +3 unit tests; live e2e drove the REAL chain-runner+digest-runner (2-step chain, step 2 degraded -> stoppedEarly -> digest returned allFailed). 2184 green. call-tested: partial (real modules, stubbed agent — pure orchestration logic, no anvil needed).

screenshot tool gained fullPage: "screenshot the whole/entire/full page" now captures top-to-bottom, not just the viewport fold. anvil already supported ?fullPage=true (actions.ts page.screenshot({fullPage})); threaded it through relay screenshot(url,fullPage) [+bumped timeout 20s->35s for tall renders], the agent tool schema + dispatch (fullPage:true), the BrowserBackend interface, and /help. +1 unit test. LIVE e2e drove real anvil on a long Wikipedia page: viewport 281KB vs fullPage 1.19MB (4.25x) - whole page captured. 2185 green. call-tested: TRUE (live anvil).

Multi-page browse shipped: new anvil scrapePaged(url,maxPages) reads a listing, finds the next/more/older pager IN the rendered DOM (rel=next, else an anchor whose text/aria-label matches next|more|older|>>|», never previous), follows it reusing ONE session, accumulates labeled page text; capped 1-5 pages (default 3) + 45s budget, loop-guarded (seen-set) + SSRF-checked on each next URL. New agent tool scrape_pages (url,maxPages) + dispatch (clamps 1-5, reports pages read so the model doesn't overclaim) + BrowserBackend.scrapePaged + SYSTEM_PROMPT + /help. scrape() unchanged. +4 unit tests. LIVE e2e drove real anvil on Hacker News: followed More -> 3 distinct pages (news, ?p=2, ?p=3), 12.3K chars vs 4.2K single-page (2.95x). 2188 green. call-tested: TRUE (live anvil, real pagination).

Infinite-scroll capture shipped: new anvil scrapeScroll(url,maxScrolls) navigates, dismisses consent, scrolls to the bottom repeatedly (900ms settle per step) until the page stops growing / cap / 45s budget, then reads the fully-expanded text. Capped 1-10 scrolls (default 5). New agent tool scroll_feed (url,maxScrolls) + dispatch (clamps, reports scrolls done so the model doesn't overclaim) + BrowserBackend.scrapeScroll + SYSTEM_PROMPT + /help. +2 unit tests. LIVE e2e on quotes.toscrape.com/scroll (real infinite-scroll): plain scrape 1492 chars (~first 10) vs scrolled 6x -> 12181 chars (8.16x, all items loaded). 2190 green. call-tested: TRUE (live anvil). This completes the anvil browse-depth backlog (pagination + full-page shot + scroll all done).

Structured list extraction across pages shipped. New extractListResult(llm,text,fields,limit) asks the LLM for a JSON ARRAY of row-objects, normalized to the requested fields, deduped by the first field, all-null rows dropped, capped 1-50. New extract_list tool (url,fields,limit,maxPages) gathers across pagination via scrapePaged (default 2 pages) then extracts rows — the real "5 cheapest / 20 newest with price+link" errand, returning clean rows not a text wall. +6 unit tests. ALSO fixed a real pagination-detector bug found in live e2e: NEXT_PAGE_SCRIPT required an EXACT label match so "Next →"/"Next »" (arrow-suffixed, the common case) was NOT followed — now strips trailing/leading arrow glyphs before matching (also strengthens the shipped scrape_pages). LIVE e2e: quotes.toscrape.com 2 pages gathered -> real Gemini extracted 8 {author,quote} rows across pages. 2196 green. call-tested: TRUE.

extract_list now gathers from an infinite-scroll feed, not just pagination: when scrapePaged finds no next link (pages===1) it auto-falls back to scrapeScroll(5) to expand the feed before row extraction. Closes the gap for scroll-loaded listings/job boards. Tool description + dispatch note ("from scrolling (Nx)") updated. +2 unit tests (fallback fires on pages===1; NOT when multi-page gathered). LIVE e2e: quotes.toscrape.com/scroll (no pager) -> pagination saw 1 page -> scroll 5x (10K chars) -> Gemini extracted 10 distinct {author,quote} rows. 2198 green. call-tested: TRUE.

NOT A GAP (verified, not built). Assumed pdf() clipped a long page like screenshot did, but anvil pdf() uses page.pdf({format}) which paginates the ENTIRE page across paper pages by default. Live probe: example.com -> 1 page/22KB, long Wikipedia -> 7 pages/676KB, whole content captured. No fix needed; avoided shipping filler. Marked not-needed.

extract_list can now hand back its rows as a downloadable CSV (extract-list-csv): when the user says csv/spreadsheet/export, the extracted rows are serialized via the shared rowsToCsv (reused from compare) + attached as list.csv instead of pasted as JSON. Header=fields, one row per item. Tool description + /help updated. +2 unit tests (CSV attached on request; NOT attached otherwise). 2200 green. call-tested: false (offline unit; pure serialization of already-live-verified extraction).

probes.note: Seeded from the inline 3-lens gap analysis run at the end of the product-loop session (subagent cap 200/200 blocked the parallel AUDIT agents, so lenses were run inline over schedule-runner/alert-runner/chain-runner/agent/handler/anvil). Keyless-tool surface confirmed exhausted. Real remaining depth gaps: browse reads ONE page only (no pagination/scroll/crawl — grep=0), screenshot is viewport-only (anvil.ts:463), and non-/run chain paths drop stoppedEarly (partial presented as complete). Owner picked the anvil-depth direction; these 4 are the starting backlog. In-place schedule EDIT (alerts retune but reminders can't) was also found — parked for a reliability pass, not this browse-depth loop.

Depth trio complete (pagination, full-page screenshot, infinite-scroll — all live-verified). Next depth tier surfaced while building: (1) the multi-page tools return RAW concatenated page text; a listing errand ("5 cheapest", "20 newest") would be far stronger if the agent EXTRACTED structured rows across the gathered pages (title/price/link) instead of the model re-parsing a wall of text — pairs scrape_pages/scroll_feed with the existing extract path. (2) full-page PDF: pdf() exists but, like screenshot was, likely renders one viewport/print-page; "save the whole thread/article as PDF" wants the full scroll. Seeded both. Owner-gated confirm-to-act multi-step chains + in-place schedule edit still parked.
Live e2e caught the arrow-label pagination miss (quotes.toscrape uses "Next →"); fixed in NEXT_PAGE_SCRIPT. Confirms the value of driving REAL sites, not just mock pages.

Browse-depth surface now thorough: pagination (link, arrow-suffixed), infinite-scroll, full-page screenshot, cross-page structured extraction (extract_list), CSV export. pdf-fullpage verified NON-issue (page.pdf paginates whole page already). Remaining depth gap surfaced: a click-driven <button>Load more</button> that fetches+appends items is NEITHER a link pager (NEXT_PAGE matches load-more only as <a href>) NOR scroll — a common listing pattern still yields page one. Seeded load-more-button. Also: extract_list dedups by FIRST field only, so two genuinely different items sharing a title collapse — minor, seeded as a refinement.
